sections.h2: Cape Girardeau County at a glance
sections.html:
Cape Girardeau County sits on the Mississippi River in the southeast corner of the state. Cape Girardeau is its biggest city and Jackson holds the courthouse. The July 2025 estimate puts the population at 83,999. Owners live in 66.8% of the homes, so about one house in three is a rental, and many local sellers are landlords with tenants. Their tax bills follow the same rules as everyone else's.

Buyers shop by school district, and that also shapes the levy on a bill. Jackson R-II, Cape Girardeau Public Schools No. 63, Delta R-V, Oak Ridge R-VI and Nell Holcomb R-IV all reach into the county. Look at the district printed on your statement to see which one you pay.

Four offices matter here. Three of them share the Jackson administration building at One Barton Square, and the Collector also runs a branch in the city of Cape Girardeau.

  • Assessor: 1 Barton Square, Suite 201, Jackson, 573-243-2468. Appraisal questions can go to appraisal@capecounty.us.
  • Collector: Suite 303 in Jackson, 573-243-4476, and 2311 Bloomfield Road, Suite 102, Cape Girardeau, 573-335-2606. Hours are 8:00 to 4:30 on weekdays.
  • County Clerk: 100 Court Street, Suite 301, Jackson. Appeal forms go here.
  • Recorder of Deeds: Suite 203, 573-243-8123.

Don't confuse the Treasurer (100 Court Street, Suite 202) with the Collector. The Treasurer does not take tax payments. A house inside the limits of Cape Girardeau or Jackson gets new-address requests through that city's planning office instead of the Assessor.

sections.h2: How to pay your tax bill
sections.html:
A statement is payable the day you receive it. The county treats December 31 as the final day free of late charges. Choose from these ways to pay.

  • Walk in to either Collector office and hand over cash, a check, a money order, a cashier's check or a card.
  • Use the drop boxes at the Jackson front door and south lot, or the door slot at the Bloomfield Road office.
  • By mail to One Barton Square, Suite 303, Jackson, postmarked by the end of the month you are paying in.
  • Pay online or call 1-877-690-3729 and enter jurisdiction code 3516. A service fee is added either way.

If a title company or lender needs proof of payment today, pay at the counter. An online or phone confirmation is only a confirmation, and the paid receipt follows after several days. Credit cards no longer work by phone or mail. Bills and receipts can be searched and printed from the county's tax portal by owner, parcel number or address.

Values are reset for January 1 of each odd-numbered year under RSMo 137.115, and new buildings or additions are picked up when completed. Talk to the Assessor first. A formal appeal then moves through three stages.

  1. Informal hearing: call 573-243-3123 ahead of the second Monday in July.
  2. Board of Equalization: sessions start the third Monday in July, and the County Clerk must have your signed form before the second Monday.
  3. State Tax Commission: the deadline is September 30, or 30 days after the Board decides if that is later.

The county wants proof that the January 1 value is off. Good evidence includes an appraisal from a Missouri appraiser, a broker opinion of value no more than three years old, an arm's-length sales contract from the past year, or repair and construction cost records. Foreclosure sales, tax sales and sales between relatives do not count as market evidence. Corporations, LLCs and partnerships file through an authorized agent, and at the State Tax Commission they need an attorney.

Voters passed two credits on April 7, 2026 that cap increases on the home you live in. Proposition A is a senior credit for owners 62 and older under SB 190 and SB 756. Proposition B is a general homestead credit under SB 3 for any owner who lives in the home.

  • Own the house, live in it and be the person who owes the tax.
  • Rentals, commercial parcels and farmland are left out.
  • Any delinquent tax, interest or penalty disqualifies you.
  • Applications are taken February 1 through April 15, and the 2027 cutoff is April 15, 2027.

You see the credit as a reduction on the November statement, not as a check. It stays with the owner and the house. When title transfers it ends, so you lose it at closing and your buyer must apply fresh. Ask about it at homestead@capecounty.us or 573-987-5010. The state statute is RSMo 137.1050. A different program, the Missouri Property Tax Credit claim, uses Form 948 signed by the Assessor.

sections.h2: Delinquent taxes and the August tax sale
sections.html:
The county auctions delinquent land on the fourth Monday of August (RSMo 140.150). Recent auctions started at 10:00 a.m. on the Administration Building's third floor, and the next is in August 2027. The parcel list is posted on the Collector's page and gets shorter as owners pay.

Before listing a parcel, the Collector mails the record owner a first-class notice, and adds a certified-mail notice when assessed value tops $1,000. Never getting the letter does not wipe out the debt. If your land sold in 2025, phone 573-243-4476 and ask the Collector to figure the redemption amount for a specific date.

A penalty starts on any tax left unpaid after January 1. Once land is on the back tax book, RSMo 140.100 sets interest at 18 percent per year of delinquency. Until the moment of sale, you can clear the account by paying the Collector the back tax plus penalty, interest and costs.

sections.h2: Selling with taxes and recording a deed
sections.html:
Start by looking up your parcel on the Collector's portal and the Assessor's real estate search. Check that the owner name is right and see whether a balance is open. Any amount owed can come out of your sale proceeds at closing through the title company, which matters because the tax sticks to the land, not the person.

The Recorder's office in Jackson files the deed. Recording and marriage license fees rose $2 on August 28, 2026, and the fee on a document is split among county and state funds. Phone 573-243-8123 for today's deed fee so your closing check is correct.

Cash Home Buyers makes offers on Cape Girardeau County houses that carry back taxes, an inherited title or sitting tenants. The closing agent pays the tax line from the price. Because no mortgage lender is involved, there is no lender appraisal or repair list to clear first.

faqs.q: Where do I pay property tax in Cape Girardeau County?
faqs.a: At the Collector's offices in Jackson (One Barton Square, Suite 303) or Cape Girardeau (2311 Bloomfield Road, Suite 102), in a drop box, by mail, online or by phone. Call 573-243-4476 or 573-335-2606 with questions.

faqs.q: What is the due date for real estate tax?
faqs.a: Bills are due on receipt, and December 31 is the last day before late charges. A mailed payment needs a postmark no later than the end of the month you are paying in.

faqs.q: How late can I appeal an assessment?
faqs.a: Get signed forms to the County Clerk before the second Monday in July. Hearings begin the third Monday, and a State Tax Commission appeal is due September 30 or 30 days after the Board rules, whichever comes later.

faqs.q: Did the county pass a homestead tax credit?
faqs.a: Yes. Voters approved a senior credit and a general homestead credit on April 7, 2026. Applications for 2027 open February 1 and close April 15, 2027, and delinquent taxes disqualify an applicant.

faqs.q: Does the tax credit transfer when I sell?
faqs.a: No. The credit is tied to the primary residence and the owner who applied, so it does not move to a new home or a new owner. A buyer who qualifies must apply separately.
